
=== story.oldMillRoad ===
TRIAL 26 CRS 005000 · State of North Carolina v. Belinda Park
  Charges: Felony Death by Vehicle; Reckless Driving
  Defendant: Belinda Park, 29, Line cook; priors: 0; Released on a $225,000 secured bond with electronic monitoring.
  TEMPLATE story.oldMillRoad
  Summary: At about 11:52 p.m. on 23 December, Belinda Park's Honda Civic crossed the center line on a curve on Old Mill Road outside Bayard and struck a Toyota Corolla head-on. The Corolla's driver, Alex Fitzgerald, 34, a nurse driving home from a twelve-hour shift, died at the scene. Belinda Park, a line cook at Riverside Grill, had stayed after closing that night. A hospital blood test about ninety minutes after the crash and a second, State Crime Laboratory test about three hours after it disagree on whether Park was over the legal limit when the cars collided. Park says a deer came out of the tree line and she swerved.
  Verdicts: Felony Death by Vehicle: notGuilty; Reckless Driving: guilty
  Form of judgment: PJC
  [Prayer for judgment continued] Prayer for judgment is continued. No sentence is imposed. | The finding of guilt remains and will count as a prior conviction.
  [Monetary obligations] Court costs: US$213.00 | Restitution: US$15,000.00 | Appointed attorney fees: US$1,600.00 | Attorney appointment fee: US$60.00 | State Crime Laboratory fee: US$600.00 | Total: US$17,473.00
  [Victim notification] The District Attorney's victim-witness legal assistant will notify the victim of the judgment and of any release, appeal, or post-conviction hearing (N.C. Const. art. I, § 37).
  Reaction: District Attorney Dolores Khalil: "We respect the court's authority, but we asked for more, and we think the facts called for it."
  Reaction: Percy Renfrow: "The court saw a person, not just a file. We're grateful."
  Reaction: Alex Fitzgerald's father, outside the courtroom: "We'll be watching to make sure every condition is followed."
  News: Guilty: Park case ends in conviction — A Hollis County judge has convicted Belinda Park on 1 of 2 counts of reckless driving, and imposed a prayer for judgment continued, with no sentence imposed. At about 11:52 p.m. on 23 December, Belinda Park's Honda Civic crossed the center line on a curve on Old Mill Road outside Bayard and struck a Toyota Corolla head-on. The judgment includes US$17,473.00 in fines, fees, costs, and restitution.

TRIAL 26 CRS 005010 · State of North Carolina v. Antonia Beaumont
  Charges: Embezzlement ($100,000 or more)
  Defendant: Antonia Beaumont, 46, School bus mechanic; priors: 14; Held in the Hollis County jail on a $250,000 secured bond for 74 days.
  TEMPLATE story.churchBooks
  Summary: For six years Antonia Beaumont, a school bus mechanic for Hollis County Schools, served as the volunteer treasurer of Cedar Hill United Methodist Church in Wexley. When a new trustee asked for the building fund statements, $112,400 was gone, moved over three years in 41 checks and transfers to an account in the name of "DL Property Services." Beaumont says Pastor Harold Peebles approved every payment as short-term loans to the contractor rebuilding the fellowship hall, and that the paperwork was handshakes. The pastor, now retired and in poor health, says no such arrangement existed.
  Verdicts: Embezzlement ($100,000 or more): guilty
  [Count 1: Embezzlement ($100,000 or more)] Class C Felony, prior record level VI | Presumptive range | Minimum 117, maximum 153 months. Active: committed to the custody of the N.C. Department of Adult Correction.
  [Commitment] Minimum term to be served before the defendant is eligible for release: 117 months (9 yr 9 mo). | Maximum term: 153 months. Earned time can move release toward the minimum, never below it; post-release supervision follows release. | Credit for 74 days already served in pretrial confinement (G.S. 15-196.1). | Projected release: no earlier than 3 June 2036, and no later than 3 June 2038. | Upon release, the defendant will serve a period of post-release supervision (G.S. 15A-1368.2).
  [Monetary obligations] Court costs: US$213.00 | Total: US$213.00
  Reaction: ADA Paulette Edmondson: "This is a fair result under the sentencing laws, and it's about public trust."
  Reaction: Harvey Chandler: "It's a hard day. We'll be talking with Beaumont about next steps."
  Reaction: A relative of Beaumont's: "We'll be waiting when it's over."
  News: Verdict in ‘$112,000 and a Handshake’ case: guilty — Superior Court Judge Hale found Antonia Beaumont, 46, guilty, and imposed 117 to 153 months in prison, ending a case that began with an arrest in Wexley. According to court records, for six years Antonia Beaumont, a school bus mechanic for Hollis County Schools, served as the volunteer treasurer of Cedar Hill United Methodist Church in Wexley. Reaction outside the courthouse was split. A relative of Beaumont's: "We'll be waiting when it's over." ADA Paulette Edmondson: "This is a fair result under the sentencing laws, and it's about public trust." Harvey Chandler: "It's a hard day. We'll be talking with Beaumont about next steps." Deputies led Beaumont out a side door. Counting 74 days already served, the earliest possible release is 3 June 2036.

TRIAL 26 CRS 005760 · State of North Carolina v. Floyd Register
  Charges: First-Degree Murder; First-Degree Murder; First-Degree Kidnapping; First-Degree Kidnapping
  Defendant: Floyd Register, 43, Long-haul truck driver; priors: 1; Held in the Hollis County jail on a $500,000 secured bond for 106 days.
  TEMPLATE story.truckStopKiller
  Summary: Seven months apart, two women who hitchhiked from truck stops were found strangled behind truck stops in North Carolina: Shayla Shah, 23, behind a stop on I-40 near Wexley, and Jade Spivey, 29, behind one on I-95. Both had zip-tie marks on their wrists. The electronic logging device in Floyd Register's tractor-trailer puts his truck at both stops within an hour of each woman's last sighting. TRIAL 26 CRS 006050 · State of North Carolina v. Nestor Willoughby
  Charges: Involuntary Manslaughter; Obstruction of Justice; Simple Assault
  Defendant: Nestor Willoughby, 21, College junior and fraternity pledge master; priors: 4; Held in the Hollis County jail on a $25,000 secured bond for 27 days.
  TEMPLATE story.hazingDeath
  Summary: On 12 April, Casimir Parnell, 19, a pledge at a fraternity near the university in Dunmore Mills, was made to run a "gauntlet" of drinking stations, downing nearly a bottle and a half of vodka in under two hours. His blood alcohol later measured 0.36. He fell headfirst down the basement stairs. Brothers carried him to a couch. The house's own security cameras show him struggling for twelve hours: falling, trying to stand, hitting his head again, while brothers walked past. At one point Willoughby slapped him and poured a cup of liquid on his face. No one called 911 until the next morning. He died of a ruptured spleen and brain injuries.
